_meta.project: instex IMAGER mode presets -- space wide-field imagers: Euclid VIS, Roman WFI, JWST NIRCam (SW and LW as separate presets)
_meta.companion: data/imaging/space_wide.md (same content as Markdown). Structure follows data/round4/mosfire.json: params/performance entries carry value, unit, src, loc, quote, optional stage/kind/derived/note and alternatives. Top-level "presets" summarises the explorer inputs per preset.
_meta.rule: Every value carries src (key into sources), loc and a short verbatim quote from the saved document. DERIVED = arithmetic done here from sourced values (shown). alternatives = other sourced values (conflicts). Every quote was machine-checked against the saved file's extracted text (pdftotext -layout and -raw per page; tag-stripped HTML; raw YAML/XML).
_meta.quote_normalisation: Unicode NFKC; dashes, minus signs, curly quotes, primes and tildes normalised; whitespace collapsed; line-end hyphenation joined; table rows quoted as cells (HTML table cells joined by " | "); ' ... ' joins non-adjacent pieces; a few table quotes match only after removing whitespace (flagged "nospace" by the checker). PDF page numbers in loc are the page index of the saved PDF.
_meta.model: DIRECT = detector at a focus of effective focal ratio F (f_eff = F x D). REIMAGED = ideal collimator f_col = F_tel x W, pupil of diameter W, ideal camera f_cam, effective focal ratio f_cam / W.

euclid_vis.title: Euclid / VIS (visible imager at the direct, f/20 focus of the 1.2 m Korsch three-mirror anastigmat; 36 e2v CCD273 4k x 4k CCDs in a 6 x 6 mosaic; single broad band 530/550-920 nm, no filter wheel)
euclid_vis.recommended_preset: DIRECT imager. D = 1.2 m (entrance pupil = aperture stop at M1; R16 Table 5 "Entrance Pupil Ø1200 mm"), eps = 0.33 (DERIVED: 0.395 m central obstruction by M2 in the ERO pupil model / 1.2 m; no published obscuration ratio), F = 20.73 (DERIVED: as-built focal length 24.87 m from EC2 Table 2 / 1.2 m; the design is "F/20.42" with 24.5 m and EC2 says "an f/20 beam"), f_eff = 24.87 m (EC2 Table 2: "Image scale 1 arcsec = 120.57 µm"). Primary focal ratio: NOT FOUND. Detectors: 36 CCD273-84, each 4096 columns (width) x 4132 rows (height) of 12.0 um pixels; rows = [6, 6, 6, 6, 6, 6], all rows centred and aligned (no offsets). Gaps between active silicon: 1.56 mm = 130 px = 12.9" between CCDs within a row (width direction) and 7.82 mm = 652 px = 64.9" between rows (height direction, readout registers) (DERIVED from EC2 Table 2 active-area dimensions; RB11 design: "7.8 mm between readout registers, and 1.6 mm in the other dimension"). Validate: 0.100"/px (EC2 Table 2; model 12/120.57 = 0.0995"/px), array 0.775 x 0.697 deg = 0.540 deg^2 enclosing rectangle including gaps (model 0.7755 x 0.6974 deg), 609,288,192 pixels, fill factor 0.861 (active-only area 0.466 deg^2, DERIVED).

not_found: A published central-obscuration ratio: only the ERO pupil-model input (0.395 m obstruction on a 1.21 m M1, ERO App. D), the bare M2 size (350 mm, R16) and two collecting areas (0.9926 m^2 EC1, 1.006 m^2 R16). eps = 0.33 is DERIVED.

The primary-mirror focal ratio (no M1 radius of curvature or focal length in any saved source); only the M1-M2 distance 1756 mm (R16). Gaspar Venancio et al. 2014 (SPIE 9143, cited by EC1/EC2 for the optical design) was not obtained.
Exit-pupil diameter at the dichroic: only the dichroic plate size (117 mm, R16). Not needed for a DIRECT preset.
Per-gap measured values: the 1.56 / 7.82 mm gaps are DERIVED from the EC2 Table 2 enclosing-rectangle dimensions and the pixel counts; RB11 gives 1.6 / 7.8 mm as the design.
conflicts: Focal length / focal ratio: 24.87 m as built (EC2 Table 2, with 1" = 120.57 um) vs 24.5 m / F/20.42 design (R16, RB11; N26 N = 20.4167) vs "an f/20 beam" (EC2 text).
Pixel scale: 0.100"/px (EC2 Table 2, EC1) vs 0.0995"/px implied by the same table's 120.57 um/" (DERIVED).

Field: 0.775 x 0.697 deg = 0.540 deg^2 active-array rectangle (EC2 Table 2) vs 0.787 x 0.709 deg^2 (EC2 Sec. 2.2, telescope field) vs 0.787 x 0.700 deg (R16 design) vs ~0.54 deg^2 (EC1); 0.466 deg^2 active silicon only (DERIVED).
Gaps: 1.56 / 7.82 mm (DERIVED from EC2 Table 2) vs 1.6 / 7.8 mm (RB11 design) vs 0.5 mm package spacing (EC2 Table 2; not the active-area gap).
Central obstruction: 0.33 (ERO pupil model, DERIVED) vs 0.29 (bare M2 / pupil, DERIVED) vs 0.33-0.35 (collecting-area upper limits, DERIVED).
notes: Orientation: EC2 Table 2 lists the 4132-row direction as "height" (0.775 deg across the array) and the 4096-column direction as "width" (0.697 deg). The readout registers lie at the top and bottom of every CCD, hence the wide (7.8 mm) gap between rows and the narrow (1.6 mm) gap within a row.
The VIS band (550-900/920 nm, depending on source) is set by the dichroic, the FoM1/FoM2 low-pass coatings, the FoM3 band-pass coating and the CCD QE; there is no filter wheel (EC1, EC2).
The 6 x 6 CCDs are 12 readout-electronics blocks of three CCDs; two blocks form a "slice" = one row of six CCDs; one of each pair is mounted upside down (EC2 Sec. 3.1).

roman_wfi.title: Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope / Wide Field Instrument (WFI; imaging channel at the focus of the 2.4 m three-mirror anastigmat; 18 Teledyne H4RG-10 detectors in 3 rows of 6 on an arc; element wheel at the exit pupil)
roman_wfi.recommended_preset: DIRECT imager (filters sit at the TMA exit pupil in the converging beam; no collimated space). D = 2.36 m (aperture-stop diameter; primary 2.4 m), eps = 0.30 (S15 Fig. 3-2: "SM: 30% linear obscuration from baffle", design 2015; P14: 30-31%), F = 7.9 (S15: "The f/7.9 optical system maps each pixel to 0.11 arcsec"), f_eff = 18.6 m (DERIVED 7.9 x 2.36; 0.11"/px with 10 um implies 18.75 m, f/7.95), primary f/1.2 (S15 App. B; DERIVED 1.18-1.20 from the P18 PM radius 5671.1 mm). Detectors: H4RG-10, 4088 x 4088 active pixels (4096 x 4096 with a 4-px reference border), 10 um; 18 detectors as rows = [6, 6, 6] (three rows of six), columns offset along the column direction on an arc (DERIVED from the Roman SIAF: relative to the two central columns the next columns are displaced by +97.5" and the outer columns by +334", symmetric). Gaps (DERIVED from SIAF, on sky): ~35-43" (~320-400 px, ~3.2-4.0 mm) between columns; ~83-87" (~780-820 px, ~8 mm) between rows 1 and 2; ~25-41" (~240-390 px) between rows 2 and 3. Design (S15, 2015): 2.5 mm between columns; 8.564 and 2.5 mm between rows. Validate: 0.11"/px; 0.281 deg^2 active (0.8 x 0.4 deg; ~2800" x 1400" including gaps); 300.8 Mpix active.

Gaps: 2.5 mm between columns and 8.564 / 2.5 mm between rows (S15, 2015 design) vs ~35-43" between columns and ~83-87" / ~25-41" between rows (DERIVED from the 2022 SIAF; 3.2-4.0 mm, ~8 mm, ~2.4-3.9 mm).

Field: 0.281 deg^2 excluding gaps (all) vs "0.320 square degrees (total)" (RDQ); 0.8 x 0.4 deg (GSFC, RTW) vs ~2800" x 1400" including gaps (RDD) vs 2899" x 1768" SIAF bounding box including the arc (DERIVED).
Central obscuration: 30% (S15 Fig. 3-2; P14 slide 29) vs 31% (P14 slide 28).
notes: The arc: the WFI uses an off-axis, annular part of the TMA field, so the six columns are staggered along the column direction (two central columns highest/lowest, outer columns displaced by ~334"); P14 also notes each SCA is tilted/pistoned "to match a field curvature of about 16 meters".

In the explorer rows form, the arc can be drawn as three rows of six with a per-column y offset [334, 97.5, 0, 0, 97.5, 334]"; if per-column offsets are not supported, rows [6, 6, 6] with uniform gaps (~37" columns; ~85" and ~35" rows) is the closest rectangular approximation.
Roman's pixel scale is anamorphic in the pre-flight SIAF (0.1093 x 0.1064"/px, ~2.7%), reflecting the off-axis field; the published nominal is 0.11"/px.
The 18 detectors are numbered by SCU position 1-18 (RTP photograph; SIAF WFI01-WFI18); SCA serial numbers differ (GSFC SCU-to-SCA table).

jwst_nircam.title: JWST / NIRCam (refractive reimaging camera: pickoff mirror + collimator triplet -> dichroic -> pupil wheel + filter wheel in collimated space -> SW (0.6-2.3 um) or LW (2.4-5.0 um) camera triplet; two identical modules A and B side by side)
jwst_nircam.recommended_preset: Two presets (SW, LW), both REIMAGED. Common: D = 6.6 m (entrance-pupil diameter, MC23; circumscribed 6.64 m, flat-to-flat 6.575 m, nominal ~6.5 m, area-equivalent 5.7 m; 18 hexagonal segments), eps = 0.20 (DERIVED: the empty central segment position, ~1.334 m flat-to-flat / 6.6 m; secondary mirror alone 0.74/6.6 = 0.11; no published ratio), F_tel = 19.91 (DERIVED: EFL 131.4 m / 6.6 m; published "f/20"), f_tel = 131.4 m, telescope = TMA (primary f/1.20 DERIVED from RoC 15879.7 mm). Pupil W = 31.14 mm (H05 Table 3 predicted internal pupil diameter; requirement "31 ± 1 mm"; G10/D17 "31 mm"), f_col = F_tel x W = 620.0 mm (DERIVED). SW: f_cam = 18 x 31.14 = 560.5 mm (DERIVED from H05 "f/18 cone"), effective f/18; 8 HAWAII-2RG, 2040 x 2040 light-sensitive (2048 x 2048 with 4-px reference border), 18 um; rows = [4, 4] (each module a 2 x 2 block; modules A and B side by side), gaps ~4-5" (~130-160 px, ~2.3-2.9 mm) inside a module and ~42-44" between modules. Validate SW: 0.031"/px (model 0.03125), 2 x 2.2' x 2.2' = 9.7 arcmin^2 (5.1' x 2.2' with the module gap). LW: f_cam = 9 x 31.14 = 280.3 mm (H05 "f/9 cone"), effective f/9; 2 HAWAII-2RG (one per module), 2040 x 2040, 18 um; rows = [2], module gap ~45-48". Validate LW: 0.063"/px (model 0.0625), 2 x 2.2' x 2.2'. Alternative f_cam from the measured scales: 565.1 mm (SW, 0.031"/px) and 278.1 mm (LW, 0.063"/px).

A published JWST linear central-obscuration ratio: eps = 0.20 is DERIVED from the segment size and the empty central position (MC23); the secondary alone gives 0.11.
